Italy to Austria: Your army count is 11 units against our 4 centers, and you lead the board. Italy wants real peace, but your Tyrol and Vienna armies are a standing threat to Venice. Will you pull A Tyr back from Venice's border this fall, and will you hold A Tri rather than strike Venice or Tunis? Answer plainly.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1946: I am down to three centers and have no wish to fight you while England and Italy grow. My A Con, A Ank and A Smy will hold and stay out of Bulgaria. Confirm your A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will not move on Constantinople, Ankara or Smyrna this fall, and we can both keep our Balkan borders quiet.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1946: My Con, Ank and Smy hold this fall, and I will not move toward Apulia or Tunis. Austria is the leader and the threat to both of us. Tell me your exact fall orders for Venice and Trieste so we can judge whether pressure on Austria is real this season.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1946: A Tyr will not move to Venice this fall, and A Tri will hold rather than strike Venice or Tunis. Keep your fleets and armies home and we stay at peace. Break that and I will respond in kind.

Austria to France, Fall 1946: A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil will not enter Burgundy or Marseille this fall. They move only in the east. Keep A Par, F Mar and A Bur on your side of the border and a western peace line is workable. Break it and I answer.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1946: A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will hold this fall and will not move on Constantinople, Ankara or Smyrna. Keep your units out of Bulgaria and we stay quiet. Restraint goes both ways.

I confirm F PRU and F BAL will stay out of Warsaw and Silesia this fall, as will F BER and F KIE; A DEN will stay out of Sweden. I expect A SIL and A MUN to remain out of my centers. I want the northern standstill maintained.

A LON is an army, so I can order A LON-WAL this fall; F NWG is already in Norway, not the North Sea, and I will keep it away from French centers. Please commit to A BUR-MUN and A BEL-RUH, with A PAR supporting the attack on Munich. Austria remains the immediate solo threat.

France to England: I am not attacking Munich on your word. Your fleets still sit in the North Sea and A Lon has not moved to Wal. Show F Nth to Nwg and A Lon-Wal in the orders you actually submit, and then we can talk about Austria. Until then my units stay home.

Italy to France: Confirmed. A Ven and A Rom hold this fall, and my fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia. F Mar and A Spa staying out of Tunis and Naples is appreciated. I will tell you before any Italian army enters Tyrol. Please keep A Bur in place until Austria's Munich units are clearer.

Italy to Turkey: Fall 1946 Italy holds A Ven and A Rom, with A Nap and A Tun holding too. No move toward Smyrna or Constantinople from us. Austria is the leader we both must check. Once you see Austrian units shift south, let us talk about Bulgaria and Greece coordination.

Italy to England: Austria is the leader, but my fall army stays in Venice to guard against Tyrol and Trieste, so no Ven-Tri this season. Keep your northern fleets out of the Mediterranean and Italian waters, and we both stay clear. Press Kiel and Denmark if you can.

Turkey to England: Your requests keep naming Bulgaria while your own fleets stay idle, so I will not move A Con or A Ank. Turkey has three centers and needs every unit to survive. If you want Austria pressured, order A Ber or F Den toward Kiel or Munich in writing, and we can discuss Bulgaria next spring. Until then Con, Ank and Smy hold.

Austria to England, Spring 1947: Your new F LON and fleets at BER, KIE, PRU and NTH are a standing threat to my north. I hold A SIL and A MUN out of your centers while the standstill holds. Tell me now if F PRU or F HEL moves toward Warsaw or Silesia. Any move into Berlin or Kiel ends our peace.

Austria and England are tied at 11, so Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Please commit A BUR-MUN supported by A BEL, and A PAR-BUR; I will order A KIE-MUN to add pressure. Are you willing to make these exact moves?

Austria has 11 centers and is seven from a solo. Please use A VEN-TYR this spring to pressure its flank; A VEN-TRI faces Austrian A TRI and may bounce. Which Austrian center will you target? I will keep English units away from Italian centers and waters.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat at 11 centers. Can you commit A CON-BUL supported by A ANK, and move A ARM-SEV? Please name the exact orders you can make this spring; coordinated pressure could prevent an Austrian win.

France to England: Spring 1947, I see F Nth still in the North Sea and A Lon not yet moved to Wal. Show F NTH-NWG or Baltic and A LON-WAL in your submitted orders, then I will discuss Munich. Until then my units stay home. Which fleet is taking the Channel now?

Italy to Austria, Spring 1947: You hold 11 centers and every turn you keep armies on my northern border. Tell me plainly whether A Tyr or A Tri will move toward Venice or Trieste this spring. Italy will hold A Ven, A Rom and A Nap at home while your moves stay clear of Italian centers.

Italy to France, Spring 1947: Austria remains the leader we must check. Will you commit A Bur-Mun or A Par-Bur against Munich this spring? My fleets stay out of Iberia and Marseille, and I want your word that F Mar and A Spa stay out of Tunis and Naples.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1947: Are you moving against Austria through Bulgaria or Greece this spring? Italy holds A Ven, A Rom, A Nap and A Tun with no move toward Smyrna or Constantinople. Confirm your exact orders so we can judge joint pressure on Austria's Balkan armies.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1947: I have three centers and need to survive. My A Con, A Ank and A Arm will hold this spring and stay out of Bulgaria, Armenia-to-Sevastopol aside. Confirm your Balkan units will not enter Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna. Mutual restraint keeps us both alive while England and Italy grow.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1947: My Con, Ank and Arm hold this spring. I will not move toward Apulia or Tunis. Please confirm your fleets stay out of the Aegean and Ionian waters near Smyrna. If Austria turns south against Greece, we can coordinate pressure then.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1947: A Tyr and A Tri will hold this spring. No Austrian unit moves toward Venice, Trieste or Tunis. Keep A Ven, A Rom and A Nap at home and we remain at peace. Break that and I will respond.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1947: A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will hold this spring. No Austrian unit enters Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna. Keep your units out of Bulgaria and Serbia, and keep A Arm away from Sevastopol. Mutual restraint works for both of us.

I will order F NTH-NWG and A LON-WAL; no fleet is taking the Channel. I will also send A KIE-MUN. Please attack Munich with A BUR-MUN: A KIE can support it if needed, but A BEL and A PAR cannot support that move. Can you commit to BUR-MUN?

F PRU and F HEL will not move toward Warsaw or Silesia; fleets cannot enter either territory. I intend to keep the northern standstill, and expect A MUN and A SIL to stay out of my centers. Let’s avoid moves into Berlin or Kiel.

France to Italy, Spring 1947: I will keep F Mar and A Spa out of Tunis and Naples this spring, as agreed. I am not committing A Bur-Mun yet; Austria's Munich units are still in place and I need them to move away first. Keep your fleets out of Iberia and Marseille, and tell me before any Italian army enters Tyrol.

France to England: Your fleets still have not shown F Nth to Nwg and A Lon to Wal in your actual orders, so I will not commit A Bur-Mun or A Par-Bur on words. Show the withdrawal first. If you do, I will discuss Munich afterward. Until then my units stay home.

Italy to Turkey: Confirmed, my fleets stay out of the Aegean and Ionian waters near Smyrna, and I have no move toward Constantinople. Italy holds A Ven, A Rom, A Nap and A Tun this spring. If Austria turns south against Greece, I will coordinate with you. Please confirm your Bulgaria plan in writing before we commit.

Italy to England: I am weighing A Ven-Tyr against Austria's flank, but Tri is too costly this spring. I will tell you my final orders before they are locked. Please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean and Italian waters, and press Kiel and Denmark as agreed.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1947: My Con, Ank and Arm hold this spring; no move toward Apulia, Tunis or the Aegean from me. Your fleets stay out of Smyrna and Constantinople waters, and we keep Ionian and Aegean borders quiet. If Austria turns south into Greece, I will consider joint action then, and I want your exact orders for Venice and Trieste first.

Turkey to England, Spring 1947: No Con-Bul this spring. You have named Bulgaria for three seasons while your fleets never reached Kiel or Munich. Put A Ber or F Den toward Kiel or Munich in writing, unit by unit, and I will reconsider Bulgaria for fall. Until then Con, Ank and Arm hold.

Austria to England, Fall 1947: Your fleets at BER, KIE and LVN are close to my northern centers. Tell me plainly if F BER, F KIE or A LON plans to move against Warsaw, Silesia or Munich this fall. I hold A SIL and A MUN out of your centers while you keep the standstill. Any attack on Berlin or Kiel ends it.

Austria and I are tied at 11, so we must stop either from reaching 18. This fall I can order A KIE-MUN; will you order A BUR to support KIE-MUN and keep your other units out of English centers? Please confirm your exact orders.

I will maintain the northern standstill this fall: no English move into Warsaw or Silesia, and I will keep my forces out of your centers except A KIE-MUN. Your A MUN is the immediate obstacle to preventing either of us from winning. Can you agree not to attack English centers?

Austria and England are tied at 11, and Austria's A MUN is the immediate threat. Can you order A VEN-TYR this fall to pressure Austria's flank? I will keep English fleets out of Italian waters and centers.

France to England, Fall 1947: Your fleets still sit in the North Sea and Nwg, and A Lon never reached Wal. Show the withdrawal in your submitted orders first. Your A Kie-Mun is no help to me unless it succeeds. I will not commit A Bur-Mun on words alone.

France to Austria, Fall 1947: Your armies have held Munich and Tyrol for two years. If A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil stay out of Burgundy and Marseille, I will keep A Par and F Mar at home. Tell me each unit's exact order this fall so we can confirm the western line.

France to Italy, Fall 1947: I keep F Mar and A Spa out of Tunis and Naples as agreed. Please confirm A Ven and A Rom hold, and that your fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia. Tell me before any Italian army enters Tyrol.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1947: You hold 11 centers and keep A Tyr and A Tri near my border. Tell me plainly whether either will move toward Venice or Trieste this fall. If you hold, Italy holds too. Better, let us discuss Balkan lines against any power that threatens us both.

Italy to England: Austria is the leader we both must check. Italy will not move A Ven-Tri this fall unless Austrian units strike south first. Keep your fleets out of Italian waters. Tell me whether your Kiel and Denmark pressure is real, and whether you will move against Munich or Silesia.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1947: Italy holds A Ven, A Rom, A Nap and A Tun. No move toward Smyrna, Constantinople or the Aegean from us. If Austria turns on Greece or Bulgaria, let us coordinate against its Balkan armies. Confirm your exact fall orders first.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1947: I hold Con, Ank and Smy this fall and will not enter Bulgaria. In return, confirm in writing your A Bul, A Gre and A Sev stay out of Ankara, Constantinople and Smyrna, and tell me your intentions for Armenia and Sevastopol.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1947: A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will hold this fall and will not enter Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna. A Arm is not in my orders. I will not move Sevastopol this turn. Keep your units out of Bulgaria and Serbia and we stay quiet.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1947: A Tyr and A Tri will hold this fall. No Austrian unit moves toward Venice, Trieste or Tunis. Keep A Ven, A Rom and A Nap at home. I am open to discussing Balkan lines against any power that threatens us both, once we see your orders.

Austria to France, Fall 1947: A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil hold this fall and will not enter Burgundy or Marseille. Keep A Par, F Mar and A Bur on your side of the line and we stay at peace in the west. Break it and I will answer.

Austria to England, Fall 1947: I will hold A Mun and A Sil this fall and will not attack English centers. Your fleets at BER, KIE and LVN are a concern. Keep F BER, F KIE and A LON out of Warsaw, Silesia and Munich, and the standstill can hold.

This fall I will not move against Warsaw or Silesia, and A LON-WAL is not an attack on your centers. I will order A KIE-MUN; your A MUN is the immediate obstacle to preventing either of us from reaching 18. Please keep your units out of English centers, and I will keep the northern standstill elsewhere.

The pressure is real: I intend A KIE-MUN this fall, and will keep English fleets out of Italian waters and centers. Please reconsider A VEN-TYR to threaten Austria’s flank; its 11 centers make it the immediate danger. Are you willing to make that move?

This fall I will order A LON-WAL and A KIE-MUN; F NWG is already in Norway and will stay away from French centers. Please order A BUR to support A KIE-MUN, and keep your other units out of English centers. That gives us a real chance to dislodge Austria from Munich.

France to England: Your fleets are still in the North Sea and Norway, and A Lon never reached Wal. I will not support A Kie-Mun or commit A Bur on words. Show a real Channel withdrawal and a Kiel move that you actually submit, then we talk. Until then my units stay home and you keep out of Brest and Belgium.

Italy to France: Confirmed for Fall 1947. A Ven and A Rom hold, my fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia, and I expect F Mar and A Spa to stay out of Tunis and Naples. I will tell you before any Italian army enters Tyrol. Keep pressure on Munich or Burgundy so Austria cannot focus south.

Italy to England: I will not order A Ven-Tri this fall unless Austrian units strike south first. Austria is the leader we both must check, but I need your Kiel and Denmark pressure to be real, not talk. Keep English fleets out of Italian waters and Tunis approaches, and tell me which Austrian unit you will hit next.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1947: Confirmed, my Con, Ank and Smy hold this fall and I will not move toward Apulia, Tunis or the Ionian. Your fleets stay out of the Aegean. Show me A Ven-Tri or A Ven-Adr movement first; if Austria turns on Greece, we coordinate against its Balkan armies next spring.

Austria to England, Spring 1948: Your A KIE-MUN order is an attack on my center, and your fleets at BER and KIE threaten my north. Confirm now whether A KIE or F BER moves on Munich or Silesia this spring. Any move against Berlin, Kiel or Munich ends the standstill and I will act accordingly.

Let’s make a real move against Austria this spring. Please order A BUR-MUN, with A BEL S BUR-MUN; I will order A KIE S BUR-MUN. Can you commit to those exact orders and keep your units out of English centers?
Austria still has 11 centers and MUN is the key obstacle. Please order A VEN-TYR this spring to pressure its flank; I will support a French attack on MUN from KIE. Can you commit to VEN-TYR?
Please commit A CON-BUL with A ANK S CON-BUL this spring to pressure Austria’s southern flank. I will support a French attack on MUN from KIE. Are those exact orders possible for you?

France to England, Spring 1948: Your fleets are still far north and A Lon never reached Wal. I need to see F Nth-Nwg and A Lon-Wal actually ordered before I discuss Munich. Also, I will not support A Kie-Mun on words. Which units are you truly committing this spring?

France to Austria, Spring 1948: Austria holds eleven centers and is the leader. A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil staying out of Burgundy and Marseille keeps the west quiet. Tell me the exact orders of each unit this spring, and I will do the same with A Par, F Mar and A Bur.

France to Italy, Spring 1948: I keep F Mar and A Spa out of Tunis and Naples as agreed. Please confirm A Ven and A Rom hold and your fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia. Tell me before any Italian army enters Tyrol. Are you planning any move against Austria this year?

Italy to France, Spring 1948: Will you move A Bur-Mun or A Par-Bur now? Austria's Balkan and Munich units are spread thin. I keep my fleets out of Marseille and Iberia. Tell me your exact spring orders, and I'll confirm mine before we lock.

Italy to England, Spring 1948: Your fleets have kept Italian waters clear. Show me real pressure: is A Kie-Mun or A Den-Kie happening? I am not moving A Ven-Tri while Austria holds Tri and Tyr. Tell me which Austrian center you are hitting so we can judge joint pressure.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1948: Your Tyrol and Trieste units have stayed put. I will keep A Ven, A Rom and A Nap home if you keep A Tri and A Tyr clear of Venice. Confirm in writing that no Austrian unit moves south this spring.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1948: My Con, Ank and Smy hold this spring and I will not enter Bulgaria or Serbia. Confirm in writing that your A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will not move into Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna, and tell me your orders for A Sil, A Tyr and A Mun.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1948: My Con, Ank and Smy hold again. Give me your exact orders for A Ven, A Rom and A Nap. If they show real pressure on Austria's Adriatic side, I will consider coordinating against Austrian units in Greece this fall, but I need your fleets kept out of the Aegean.

Austria to France, Spring 1948: A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil hold this spring and will not enter Burgundy or Marseille. Keep A Par, F Mar and A Bur on your side and the west stays quiet. I will watch Spain and Portugal too.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1948: A Tri and A Tyr hold this spring. No Austrian unit moves toward Venice or Tunis. Keep A Nap, A Rom and A Ven home and we stay at peace. If you move on Trieste or Tyrol, I will answer.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1948: A Bul, A Gre and A Sev hold this spring and will not enter Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna. A Sil, A Tyr and A Mun hold too. Keep your units out of Bulgaria and Serbia and we stay quiet.

A KIE will support A BUR-MUN this spring; that is an attack on Munich. F BER will hold, and no English unit is moving to Silesia, Warsaw, Berlin, or Kiel. I want to keep the rest of the northern standstill, but Munich cannot remain an untouched Austrian stronghold.

I will order A KIE to support A BUR-MUN. My A WAL will hold, and F BAR will stay away from French centers; I cannot order F NTH-NWG because I have no fleet in NTH. Please order A BUR-MUN with A BEL supporting it, and keep your units out of English centers. I cannot guarantee the attack succeeds without your exact orders.

A KIE will support A BUR-MUN this spring; I am not ordering A DEN-KIE. I have no interest in Italian waters. Austria’s Munich is the center I am pressuring, and VEN-TYR would add useful pressure on Austria’s flank. Will you make that move?

France to England: Your fleets are still in the North Sea and Norway, and A Lon has not reached Wal. Words alone won't move my Burgundy army. Show F Nth-Nwg and A Lon-Wal in your submitted orders, then I'll discuss Munich. Until then I keep A Bur, A Bel and A Par at home.

France to Italy, Spring 1948: I still keep F Mar and A Spa out of Tunis and Naples, and I expect your fleets to stay out of Marseille and Iberia. My orders this spring are A Par and A Bur holding, with F Mar in place. I will tell you before any move toward Austria changes that. Please confirm A Ven and A Rom hold.

Italy to France, Spring 1948: A Ven and A Rom hold this spring, and my fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia. I will not move toward Tyrol without telling you first. Prove your intent: A Bur-Mun this spring, with A Par-Bur behind it, and I will keep Tunis and Naples locked tight. Send me your exact orders before we lock.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1948: Exact orders: A Nap holds, A Rom holds, A Ven holds this spring. No Italian fleet or army enters the Aegean, Ionian approaches to Smyrna, or Constantinople waters. If Austria moves on Greece this fall, I am ready to coordinate with you against its Balkan armies. Keep Ank and Con defensive and tell me your fall plan first.

Turkey to England: No Con-Bul this spring. Your fleets have sat idle for years while you promise Munich. Show me written orders: A Kie-Mun or F Den toward Holland or Kiel, unit by unit, and I will reconsider Bulgaria in fall. Until then Con, Ank and Smy hold.

Austria to England, Fall 1948: Your A KIE and F BER are threatening Munich and my northern centers. Confirm now that A KIE does not move to Munich and F BER stays out of Warsaw and Silesia. Otherwise I will defend Munich and respond in kind against your Berlin and Kiel.

Austria remains on 11 centers, and Munich is still the key northern obstacle. Will you order A BUR-MUN with A BEL supporting, while I order A KIE S BUR-MUN? Please keep your units out of English centers; tell me your exact orders this fall.

Austria still holds 11 centers. Will you order A VEN-TYR this fall to pressure its flank? I can support A BUR-MUN from KIE if France commits. I will keep English units out of Italian centers and waters; please confirm your intended move.

Austria remains the immediate 11-center threat. Will you order A CON-BUL with A ANK supporting this fall? I can support France's attack on Munich from KIE if France commits. Please tell me whether you will make that exact move.

France to England, Fall 1948: Your fleets are still in the North Sea and Norway, and your Kiel and Lvp armies have not moved as promised. I will not commit A Bur-Mun on words. Show a real Channel withdrawal in your submitted orders, then we discuss. Until then my units stay home and Brest and Belgium stay closed to you.

France to Austria, Fall 1948: You hold eleven centers and I hold five. I want to know your exact orders this fall, especially for A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil. If they stay out of Burgundy and Marseille, I keep A Par, F Mar and A Bur at home. I am also willing to discuss a Spain-Portugal arrangement later.

France to Italy, Fall 1948: I keep F Mar and A Spa out of Tunis and Naples. Please confirm A Ven and A Rom hold and your fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia. Tell me your exact orders before any Italian army moves toward Tyrol, and say whether you will help me hold the western Mediterranean.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1948: Italy holds A Ven, A Rom, A Nap, A Tun. Your Balkan armies outnumber us, and we have both been on the board too long without gains. Propose a clear line: you keep Tyrol and Trieste out of Venice, and I keep my fleets out of the Adriatic north. Confirm your exact fall orders first.

Italy to England, Fall 1948: Your fleets have stayed out of Italian waters, which I appreciate. Stop talking about A Ven-Tri: I am not making that move. Show me the Kiel pressure now, with A Kie-Mun or A Kie-Den-supported action, and tell me your exact fall orders so we can judge whether we are actually aligned.

Italy to France, Fall 1948: I hold A Ven, A Rom, A Nap, A Tun this fall and keep fleets out of Marseille and Iberia. Confirm your exact orders for A Bur and A Par, and tell me if Mun is being hit. Any Italian move into Tyrol will be announced to you before orders lock.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1948: My Con, Ank and Smy hold again. Austria has 11 centers and is the clear leader, so restraint helps only if it is real. Confirm in writing that A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will not enter Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna, and tell me what A Sil, A Tyr and A Mun do this fall.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1948: A Bul, A Gre and A Sev will hold this fall and will not enter Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna. A Sil, A Tyr and A Mun are being kept under review; I will not pledge their orders beyond defending my own centers. Keep your units out of Bulgaria and Serbia and we remain at peace.

Austria to France, Fall 1948: A Mun, A Tyr and A Sil hold this fall and will not enter Burgundy or Marseille. Keep A Par, F Mar and A Bur at home and the west stays quiet. A Spain-Portugal discussion can wait until we see spring results.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1948: A Tri and A Tyr hold this fall. No Austrian unit moves toward Venice or Tunis. Keep A Ven, A Rom, A Nap and A Tun away from Trieste and Tyrol and we stay at peace. Your fleets stay out of the Adriatic north, as you proposed.

F BAL is not in Berlin, and I have no English unit in a position to move on Warsaw or Silesia this turn. I will keep F BAL out of those provinces. I cannot promise that A KIE will stay out of Munich; your concentration there leaves little room for a lasting standstill.

Understood. I will order F ENG-MAO this fall as a real Channel withdrawal. I am still prepared to order A KIE S A BUR-MUN, but only if you submit A BUR-MUN and A BEL S A BUR-MUN. Please keep your units out of English centers.

A KIE-MUN is the pressure I can make this fall; I am not ordering A KIE-DEN or moving into Italian waters. Munich is heavily defended, so VEN-TYR would matter if you want to pressure Austria’s flank. Are you willing to make that move?

France to Italy, Fall 1948: My orders this fall are A Par holding, A Bur holding, F Mar holding, A Spa holding and A Bel holding. I keep F Mar and A Spa out of Tunis and Naples. Your A Ven and A Rom holding is welcome. If Austria moves on Tyrol or Venice, tell me at once, and we can discuss a joint western Mediterranean line.

Italy to France, Fall 1948: A Ven, A Rom, A Nap and A Tun all hold this fall. My fleets stay out of Marseille and Iberia, and I expect the same from you toward Tunis and Naples. I am not moving toward Tyrol now. Send your exact A Bur and A Par orders before we lock, and tell me whether Munich is being attacked.

Italy to England, Fall 1948: I am not ordering A Ven-Tri or any move into Tyrol. Thank you for keeping English units out of Italian waters. Show your Kiel pressure first: send your exact fall orders for A Kie and the fleets in the North Sea, and I will judge alignment from there.

Turkey to England: No Con-Bul this fall. You have promised Munich and Bulgaria for three seasons with nothing on the board. Show me one unit moving toward Munich or Kiel-adjacent positions in writing, such as A Kie-Mun or F Den-Kie, and I will talk about Bulgaria next year. Until then Con, Ank and Smy hold.

Austria to England, Spring 1949: Your fleets and armies at KIE, BER and BAL are poised against my north. Tell me plainly: will A KIE or F PRU move on Munich, Silesia or Warsaw this spring? If you hold, I will hold my Balkan armies and keep A Mun and A Sil defensive.
I will order A KIE S A BUR-MUN this spring. Please commit A BUR-MUN; my fleets will not move against French centers. Munich is defended, so tell me your exact supporting or diversion orders as well.

Austria remains at 11 centers and Munich is the northern obstacle. Will you finally order A VEN-TYR or another concrete move against Austria this spring? I can commit A KIE S A BUR-MUN if France attacks. I will keep English units out of Italian centers and waters.

Austria still holds Bulgaria and is tied with me at 11 centers. Will you order A CON-BUL with A ANK S CON-BUL this spring? I intend to support a French A BUR-MUN from KIE if France commits; please tell me your exact orders.

France to England, Spring 1949: Your army and fleet units are still far from Channel withdrawal, and Kiel and Lvp have not moved. I will not order A Bur-Mun on promises. Show F Eng-Mao or F Pic-Bel and A Kie-Den in your orders, and I will keep Brest and Belgium closed to you while we talk.

Italy to France, Spring 1949: Italy holds Ven, Rom, Nap, Tun this spring. Your fleets stay out of Tunis and Naples and mine stay out of Marseille and Iberia. Tell me your exact spring orders for A Bur and F Mar, and whether you are moving on Munich or Piedmont-side targets.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1949: Your 11 centers make you the target. Show me exact orders for A Sil, A Tyr and A Mun this spring, and state whether A Bul, A Gre or A Sev move. I will keep Con, Ank and Smy defensive, but I need your Balkan and Armenian intentions in writing before any further restraint.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1949: My A Bul, A Gre and A Sev hold this spring and will not enter Ankara, Constantinople or Smyrna. A Sil, A Tyr and A Mun stay defensive as well, and I will not move them into Bulgaria or Serbia. Keep your Con, Ank and Smy units home and we remain at peace. Any move against Bulgaria, Greece or Sevastopol changes this.

This spring A KIE will move to DEN, not Munich; F PRU will hold and I will not move on Silesia or Warsaw. I want to avoid a northern front while we deal with the situation in the west. Please keep A MUN and A SIL defensive and out of English centers.

I will order F ENG-MAO and A KIE-DEN this spring, and will keep my fleets out of French centers. F PIC-BEL cannot work while my F BEL occupies Belgium. I cannot support A BUR-MUN from KIE while moving it to DEN; please keep A BUR and A PAR out of English centers.

France to Italy, Spring 1949: My spring orders are A Bur holding and F Mar holding, with A Par holding. I am not moving on Munich or Piedmont this spring. I keep my fleets out of Tunis and Naples as long as yours stay out of Marseille and Iberia. Please confirm A Ven and A Rom hold, and tell me if Austria moves on Tyrol or Venice.

France to England, Spring 1949: I will not order A Bur-Mun. Your fleets are still in the North Sea and Kiel has not moved. Show F Eng-Mao or F Pic-Bel and A Kie-Den in your submitted orders, and then we can talk about Munich. Until then Brest, Belgium and Spain stay closed to you.

Italy to England, Spring 1949: I will not order A Ven-Tyr. Venice stays home while Austria's Tyrol and Trieste armies are a clear threat to us.
